items.title: ReconLegacy: migrate off Oracle 11g (extended support ending)
items.text:
Summary: The Oracle 11g host underneath ReconLegacy is running on extended support that is ending. We need a plan to move the nightly reconciliation batch off 11g before we are on an unsupported database with no patches. That is not a position I want to defend in an audit.

Background:
- ReconLegacy is Perl batch jobs on the Oracle 11g host. Cron kicks off at 02:15 ET.
- It reads SettlementEngine extracts and GLCore balances and posts the break report to #recon by 06:30.
- It has failed three times since July: the late FX rate table on 07-22, the stale-price abort after the PricingSvc incident on 08-14, and the tablespace failure on 08-27. Each one needed a manual intervention.

Scope (initial):
1. Inventory all Perl modules, cron entries, and Oracle objects (tables, packages, housekeeping jobs).
2. Pick a target. Options are a supported Oracle version as a lift-and-shift, or a rewrite onto the platform we already run for SettlementEngine and GLCore.
3. Run old and new side by side, comparing break reports for at least one full month-end.
4. Cut over and decommission the 11g host.

Asking Priya to own the estimate and the technical plan. Please flag anything that changes the shape of this.

Priority: High
Assignee: Priya Raman

--- Comment by Priya Raman ---
Thanks Sam. Some honest context before anyone puts dates on a slide.

The Oracle side is the easy part. The hard part is the Perl. Most modules are straightforward extract/match/report code. The FX adjustment module (step 4) is different. It holds years of special cases: how we treat same-day FX on settlement versus trade date, rounding tolerances by currency pair, and a fallback for when the PricingSvc snapshot lands late. Very little of it is written down anywhere except in the code and in my head. The same is true, to a lesser degree, of the month-end handling and the housekeeping scripts that keep the tablespace from filling up (the 08-27 failure).

Realistic estimate: about 3 months for a migration with a proper parallel run. That assumes no surprises, and there are always surprises with this code.

My strong recommendation is to pair someone with me before any migration work starts. Ideally that person sits with me on the nightly support rotation for a few weeks. They should learn why the code behaves the way it does, not just what it does. Otherwise we risk porting the bugs and losing the fixes.

--- Comment by Priya Raman ---
Adding one item for the inventory. The --asof re-run path I used on 08-15 needs to be preserved in whatever we build. Ops relies on it whenever upstream pricing is late.

items.title: Resignation
items.text:
Hi Sam,

This isn't an easy email to write. I'm resigning from Halcyon Ridge, and my last day will be Friday, October 9, 2026.

I've loved my time here, and I'm grateful for your support, especially over the last couple of years. I also know the timing is awkward given ITOPS-262. I want to leave ReconLegacy in as good a shape as I can.

I'd like to run knowledge-transfer sessions over the next two weeks with whoever will pick it up. The parts that are not documented anywhere are:

- The FX adjustment module (step 4): currency-pair tolerances, the settlement-date versus trade-date logic, and the late-snapshot fallback.
- The month-end manual override: what gets toggled, when, and how to back it out.
- The Oracle housekeeping scripts: tablespace cleanup, stats gathering, and the archive purge that prevents repeats of 08-27.

I'll write up as much as I can alongside the sessions and update the July runbook.

Thank you for everything. Happy to talk tomorrow about how you'd like to handle the transition.

Best,
Priya

Team, quick but urgent: besides Priya, who has ever actually worked on ReconLegacy internals? I mean the Perl jobs, the FX adjustment step, or the Oracle housekeeping, even once. I need names today please. Reply in thread or DM me.

Honestly, I've only been in there once, for a ticket where I traced a file path issue in the settlement extract load. I didn't really understand the Perl jobs beyond that. Happy to be the one who learns it, but I'd be starting close to zero.

items.title: ReconLegacy knowledge transfer #1
items.text:
Sam Okafor: Thanks for staying late, everyone. I know it's Friday at six. The goal today is the end-to-end batch flow, then the FX module and the month-end override. Tasha's here so we get the ops view of what breaks look like downstream. Priya, it's yours.
Priya Raman: Okay. Kevin, start with the crontab on the 11g host. Everything begins at 02:15 ET with one wrapper script, and it calls six steps in order. If any step exits non-zero, the wrapper stops and nothing gets posted to #recon.
Kevin Zhao: So the 06:30 post depends on every step succeeding?
Priya Raman: Yes. Step 1 pulls the SettlementEngine extract. Step 2 loads GLCore balances into staging tables. Step 3 does the match on trade id, account, and currency. Step 4 is FX adjustment. Step 5 classifies the breaks. Step 6 formats the report and posts it.
Kevin Zhao: Basic question: what happens if the settlement file is late? Does it wait?
Priya Raman: Step 1 polls for forty minutes, then aborts. That's the late-settlement failure in the runbook. You rerun from step 1 once the file lands.
Tasha Greene: From my side, that shows up as no report at 06:30. I usually ping #recon around seven if it's missing.
Priya Raman: Now step 4, which is the part nobody else has seen. It reads the FX rate table that comes from the PricingSvc snapshot. If the snapshot is older than the cutoff, the job aborts on purpose rather than computing breaks with stale rates. That's what happened after the PricingSvc incident in August, when I reran with --asof for 08-14.
Kevin Zhao: Why abort instead of using yesterday's rates?
Priya Raman: Because Tasha's team would get hundreds of false breaks and spend the morning chasing them. On July 22 the table loaded late and we got fourteen FX breaks. That was a partial load, which is worse than an abort.
Tasha Greene: Yeah, that morning was painful. All FX trades, all noise.
Priya Raman: Inside step 4 there's a tolerance hash keyed by currency pair. Majors have tight tolerances. A handful of restricted and thinly traded pairs get wider ones. There's also a branch that uses settlement-date rates instead of trade-date rates for same-day FX. That branch exists because GLCore books those on settlement date. If you change it, everything breaks.
Kevin Zhao: Is the tolerance hash in config or hardcoded?
Priya Raman: Hardcoded, unfortunately. In FxAdjust.pm, near the top. I'll comment every entry before I leave.
Sam Okafor: Can we capture which business owner approved each tolerance? We'll need that for the migration.
Priya Raman: Some of them, from old emails. I'll do my best.
Priya Raman: Last piece today is the month-end override. On the last business day, accrual entries hit GLCore after the settlement extract is cut, so the match would show false breaks. There's a flag file in the batch config directory. When it's present, step 3 excludes accrual account types and step 5 tags them for review instead of as breaks.
Kevin Zhao: Who creates the flag file?
Priya Raman: Me, manually, around six p.m. on month-end. And I remove it the next morning after Tasha confirms the accruals are in.
Tasha Greene: I didn't know that was manual. I just assumed month-end looked cleaner.
Kevin Zhao: What if someone forgets to remove it?
Priya Raman: Then real accrual breaks get hidden the next day. That's the risk. It should be automated, but it never was.
Sam Okafor: That goes on the ticket as its own item. Kevin, you'll do the October month-end flag yourself with Priya's notes, even though she's gone by then.
Kevin Zhao: Understood. Can I shadow a rerun before then?
Priya Raman: Yes. Monday I'll walk you through a --asof rerun on the test copy. We haven't touched the Oracle housekeeping scripts yet either.
Sam Okafor: Right. Realistically we need at least four more sessions before October 9: housekeeping and tablespace, a hands-on rerun, a full code read of FxAdjust.pm, and one for questions and the runbook update. I'll book them for next week. Kevin, clear your calendar as much as you can.
Kevin Zhao: Will do.
Sam Okafor: Thanks, all. Have a good weekend.

After 13 years, today is my last day at Halcyon Ridge. Thank you all for the patience, the 7 a.m. break chases, and the friendship along the way. I'll miss this place and you a lot. For anything ReconLegacy, Kevin Zhao is now your go-to, so please be kind to him while he settles in. Stay in touch! 💙
